symptom_description: Pitting corrosion on the landing gear strut near the lower bearing, approximately 2mm deep, discovered during a scheduled inspection.
diagnosis: Localized pitting corrosion consistent with moisture ingress at a worn seal. Depth is within removable limits per the applicable structural repair manual chapter.
resolution: Corrosion blended out per AC 43.13-1B corrosion removal procedure, area re-primed and sealed, seal replaced at the lower bearing to prevent recurrence.

symptom_description: Hairline crack found on the wing spar cap during a scheduled inspection, roughly 15mm long, running spanwise.
diagnosis: Fatigue crack at a stress-concentration point near a fastener hole. Non-destructive inspection (dye penetrant) confirmed crack depth was subsurface-limited.
resolution: Component referred to engineering for a stop-drill and doubler repair; aircraft grounded until repair approved and completed.

symptom_description: Dent in the fuselage skin, about 40mm across and shallow, no visible cracking, found near a ground-service door.
diagnosis: Cosmetic/minor structural dent, most likely from ground equipment contact. Depth-to-diameter ratio within allowable damage limits, no skin cracking detected.
resolution: Logged as acceptable damage per allowable-damage chart, no repair required, re-inspected at next scheduled check.

symptom_description: Fine cracking observed on a high-strength steel landing gear component after exposure to de-icing fluid over several seasons.
diagnosis: Stress corrosion cracking (SCC) consistent with sustained tensile stress combined with a corrosive environment; typical failure mode for this alloy under these conditions.
resolution: Component removed from service and replaced; adjacent components inspected for similar exposure history per fleet campaign directive.

symptom_description: Surface grains lifting and flaking on a 7075-T6 wing skin component, white residue present around fastener heads.
diagnosis: Exfoliation corrosion, a form of intergranular attack common in this alloy when protective finish has been compromised over time.
resolution: Affected material removed within allowable limits, area treated and re-finished; fastener heads re-sealed to prevent moisture entry.

symptom_description: Shallow surface scratch on a cowling panel, roughly 60mm long, does not penetrate the primer layer.
diagnosis: Cosmetic scratch from routine handling, no structural significance, does not meet the threshold for a damage report.
resolution: Touch-up paint applied, logged in the maintenance record, no further action required.

symptom_description: White powdery deposit on an aluminium panel near the wheel well, technician unsure if it is corrosion or residue.
diagnosis: Surface (Type I) corrosion, an early-stage oxidation product rather than deep pitting; typical of aluminium exposed to runway de-icing chemicals.
resolution: Deposit removed with an approved corrosion-removal compound, area inspected under magnification to confirm no pitting beneath, re-primed.

symptom_description: Multiple small pits found on a hydraulic actuator housing during teardown inspection, individual pits under 1mm deep.
diagnosis: Pitting corrosion from long-term exposure to condensation inside the housing; pit depth within acceptable removable limits for this component.
resolution: Pits blended and polished per the component maintenance manual, housing passed post-repair dimensional and pressure checks.

symptom_description: Technician query: 'Which inspection method finds subsurface cracks in aluminium?' during a routine structural check with no visible surface damage.
diagnosis: No confirmed defect from this query alone; eddy-current or ultrasonic inspection is the appropriate method for detecting subsurface cracking in aluminium structure where surface inspection shows nothing.
resolution: Eddy-current inspection scheduled as a precaution; no crack found on follow-up, aircraft returned to service.

symptom_description: Slight bowing observed in a stringer section after a hard landing report, no visible cracking or paint disturbance.
diagnosis: Minor permanent deformation consistent with an overload event below the structural damage threshold; no crack initiation detected on close visual and dye-penetrant inspection.
resolution: Component measured against engineering tolerance, found within limits, no repair required, documented for trend monitoring.

symptom_description: Yellowish discoloration around a rivet line on an engine cowling, no pitting or raised material visible.
diagnosis: Heat-related discoloration, likely from proximity to the exhaust path rather than corrosion; no material loss detected.
resolution: Area cleaned and inspected, no corrosion present, logged as cosmetic, re-checked at next inspection interval.

symptom_description: Corrosion detected around rivet heads and in skin crevices near an engine exhaust trail, moderate surface staining.
diagnosis: Corrosion accelerated by exhaust residue chemistry pooling in crevices; a known problem area per the general visual corrosion inspection guide.
resolution: Corrosion removed per approved procedure, crevices resealed, exhaust trail area added to the enhanced-frequency inspection list for this airframe.

symptom_description: Service-induced crack found in the fuselage skin near a window cutout during a heavy check, approximately 8mm long.
diagnosis: Fatigue crack originating from a stress riser at the cutout radius, a known life-limiting location for this airframe type.
resolution: Crack stop-drilled and a doubler installed per the structural repair manual; life-limit tracking updated for the affected zone.

symptom_description: Fastener hole showing slight elongation and light corrosion staining on a wing panel during a routine borescope check.
diagnosis: Combination of fretting corrosion and minor hole elongation from fastener movement; within repairable limits.
resolution: Hole oversized and a larger fastener installed per acceptable repair methods, corrosion cleaned from surrounding material, area resealed.

symptom_description: Corrosion found on a magnesium component near the auxiliary power unit, technician noted a strong chemical odor during inspection.
diagnosis: Active corrosion on a magnesium alloy, which is especially susceptible to rapid attack once the protective coating is breached; treated as urgent given the material.
resolution: Component removed and sent for overhaul rather than field repair, given magnesium's corrosion sensitivity; replacement coated component installed.

symptom_description: Dent with a shallow tear in a cowling panel from a suspected bird strike, roughly 50mm across with a small break in the material.
diagnosis: Combined impact damage: a dent with a minor material tear that exceeds the allowable-damage chart's clean-dent limits because of the break.
resolution: Panel repaired with a doubler patch per the applicable structural repair manual, rather than treated as cosmetic since the tear disqualified it from the simple allowable-damage path.

symptom_description: Cracks noted in sharp radii near a threaded landing-gear component during overhaul, technician flagged for immediate review.
diagnosis: Cracking at a stress-concentration radius on a threaded part, a documented high-risk location where cracks propagate quickly under cyclic load.
resolution: Component rejected and replaced outright rather than repaired, per guidance that cracked threaded/high-stress parts are not field-repairable.

symptom_description: Technician query: 'surface corrosion removal procedure' after finding light general corrosion across a wing walk area.
diagnosis: Widespread but shallow surface corrosion, typical of a wing walk area subject to foot traffic wearing through protective finish over time.
resolution: Corrosion removed with the daily/light-duty method per the general corrosion inspection guide, area re-coated with anti-slip protective finish.
